messages:
IncidentBot: ALERT - auth-provider-validate errors > 20% for prod auth flow (token verification failures). paging on-call. :rotating_light:
Maya K: I'm on it. Seeing login failures in Sentry and spikes in 502/503 for /oauth/token and /.well-known/jwks.json.
Li S: Confirmed. Our auth-verify service logs: `error: jwks fetch failed status=502 url=https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json` and downstream `jwt.verify: invalid signature` for many requests.
Juan R: Is this Auth0 or Okta? Which provider are customers hitting?
Maya K: Majority of traffic for the affected tenant uses Auth0 (prod-us). Okta tenants are mostly fine.
Chris P: Can we flip to cached JWKS immediately? Runbook suggests using cached keys for 30m while provider resolves.
Maya K: Doing that now. Patching auth-verify config to prefer local cache and extend TTL.
Tanya D: Heads-up: this will allow existing tokens but won't allow fresh logins that require key rotation. Customer-impact: console SSO and new sign-ins affected.
Amy C: Support is getting tickets. Some enterprise customers cannot access the admin console. Marking severity P1 and we need an incident bridge.
Maya K: Bridge started (zoom link pasted in incident channel). Notifying sales/eng leads.
Li S: Quick mitigation commands run:
```
# switch jwks to cache-first
curl -X POST "https://internal-config/api/v1/services/auth-verify/config" -d '{"jwks_mode":"cache_first","cache_ttl":1800}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-verify -n prod
```
Rollout shows 0 -> 3 pods restarting.
DeployBot: Cancelled deploy job pipeline/789 triggered earlier (blocked by auth failures).
Juan R: Checking logs from gateway: a large fraction of jwks fetches are 502 from auth host, and some 429s on the provider side. Might be a partial provider-side degradation.
Chris P: Can we add a short-term circuit breaker so auth-verify stops hammering provider and instead serves cached keys?
Maya K: Implemented circuit breaker at gateway (limit jwks fetch rate to 1/min per instance). Monitor in Datadog dashboard (link).
Tanya D: Also open a ticket with Auth0 support and link our logs/traces. Assigned to Maya and Juan.
Maya K: Ticket created: https://support.auth0.com/incidents/INC-34567 (internal note: include Sentry IDs and sample curl). Auth0 status page shows "partial outage - JWKS retrieval".
Amy C: Customer comms draft: "We're investigating an authentication provider issue affecting login and console access for some customers. We're applying mitigations and will update in 30 minutes." Approving to send.
Li S: After cache-first and circuit-breaker, token verification failures dropped to ~4% within 7 minutes. Not resolved but mitigated.
Juan R: Can we roll a fallback to our secondary token-issuer for internal console access (for admins) while public SSO is degraded?
Chris P: We have an emergency admin flow (internal-oauth) that can be enabled per-tenant. Will gate behind MFA and audit logs.
Maya K: Enabling internal-oauth for 3 impacted enterprise tenants now. Notifying their CSMs.
Tanya D: Keep logs/audit for compliance. Notify security if anyone uses emergency flow.
Maya K: Handoff note for next on-call (Li): cause likely provider-side JWKS failures causing jwt.verify errors; mitigations applied: cache-first JWKS, circuit-breaker on fetches, admin internal-oauth enabled for critical tenants, support ticket opened with Auth0, deploys paused.
Li S: Copy. Will monitor for 1hr and escalate to provider if errors climb.
IncidentBot: INCIDENT UPDATE - severity P1, status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next update in 30m or on change.
Amy C: Sent customer comms and updated status page.
Maya K: Leaving thread, handoff complete. On-call until 08:00 local handed to Li. :white_check_mark:
